Answer: D
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figures 1a and 1b) demonstrates a well-defined, oval-shaped opacity in the right mid-lung zone that has broad-based contact with the pleural surface (visible on the lateral view). The presence of air-bronchograms within this mass-like consolidation is a hallmark sign of alveolar filling, making round pneumonia the most likely diagnosis over malignancy or benign nodules which typically lack air-bronchograms.
